meta.who_this_is_for: an agent with limited usage but strong reasoning: three problems, each one blocked a whole language lane and each one has already eaten multiple failed attempts. Do not start a fourth.

state_snapshot.attempt_keep_rate: about 35 percent (13/30, 4/16, 5/13, 11/29 across the last four rounds) - most attempts are reverted by the two rules below, which is why these three problems are worth more than any single language

environment.build: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$PWD/.cargo-target CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_OPT_LEVEL=3 cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --features 'deep parser'
environment.measure: RG_LOSSES=1 RG_AUDIT=1 $BIN build /tmp/opencode/lean/corpus45/<lang> --no-cache 2>&1 | awk -F'\t' '/^loss\t/{f[$2]=1; r++} END{print length(f)" files "r" rows"}'
guards: cargo test --bin rust-graph  (must stay 256 passed / 0 failed)
self-parse: $BIN build rust-graph/src --no-cache must stay 0 files / 0 rows
rules: files down and rows up = revert
one language measured at a time, never a 45-language sweep per attempt
measure the language you touched plus the 7-corpus guard; nothing else

items.title: A brace or bracket opens a block before the call/import reader sees the statement, so no per-statement guard can reach it

evidence.tcl: 598 files / 729 rows on 1104 files (54.07%) after a full 25 measured attempts. Started this campaign at 957/957 (86.53%). Round 6 found and round 7 applied all three named root causes (is_layout skipping braced_word/command_substitution/quoted_word; proc_command recorded outside the proc scope; call_command emitting no x-events) and it still will not cross 54 percent.
evidence.clojure: 1018 files / 1454 (70.01%). A lane sat on it for three hours without a single kept attempt.
evidence.rust: the same mechanism previously blocked `use {a as b, c};` - the statement produces no event at all because the brace splits it into a block before the import reader runs. Four separate guard attempts failed on it.

tcl_loss_mix_measured_2026_11_24.reading: 73 percent of what tcl pays is the call bucket, i.e. exactly the call_command path below - this is not a spread of small bugs, it is one reader

reverted_attempts: `in_command_call` juxtaposed guard in src/expr.rs raised tcl 684 -> 817 files, reverted
round 6 attempt a029 (0 files / +59 rows) and a030 (0 files / +1001 rows), both reverted

where.brace_classifier: src/parser.rs:191 (enum BraceContext), src/parser.rs:1369 (classify_brace_context) - it exists but is only consulted for initialisers (block vs struct literal vs table constructor), never on the import or call statement path
where.tcl_call_path: src/deep_facts/mod.rs:3001 (tcl_call_command), src/deep_facts/mod.rs:6283 (dispatch on call_command), TCL_CALLS at src/deep_facts/mod.rs:501
where.layout_filter: src/deep_facts/mod.rs:1411 (is_layout) - the function every failed guard tried to work around

items.why_hard: every fix so far has been a per-statement guard, and the statement does not exist as a statement by the time the reader runs. The fix has to move up a layer: the lexer must classify the brace before it decides to open a block, and the call/import readers must consume the classified construct rather than filter tokens after the fact.
items.definition_of_done: tcl below 598 files without its rows rising above 729; clojure moves at all (below 1018) with rows not rising above 1454; rust stays at 26/27 and self-parse at 0 rows.
do_not: do not add another is_layout skip-list entry - that is the shape of all six prior failures
do not raise the loss threshold to make the percentage move
items.known_extra: tcl also exits rc=-11 (SIGSEGV) after printing its loss rows. The rows are complete before the crash, so measurement is valid, but the crash is unfixed and may be a second bug hiding in the same reader.

items.title: Unmasking one fact kind makes the row count explode, so every attempt at it gets reverted - the x-event nesting invariant is not written down anywhere
items.affected: all 45 languages, and it is the single biggest reason attempts are wasted

evidence.bash: the -flag guard turned 468 files/1,010 rows into 4,914 rows and was reverted
evidence.r: generic call_arguments turned 7,194 rows into 8,636 and was reverted
evidence.tcl: multi-word emission was reverted at 684 files/743 rows; and a round 7 call fix unmasked exactly 1,034 x-event rows in one step
evidence.zig: test_declaration / builtin_call form, reverted on the same rule
evidence.solidity: mapping_body named-parameter rule raised 159 -> 165 files, reverted

where.value_shapes: src/expr.rs - where both readers' value shapes are decided for every language, and where the reverted in_command_call guard lived
where.event_emitters: src/deep_facts/mod.rs (per-language emit arms), src/deep_facts/go.rs (shared path/form/member_name helpers)
where.reason_codes: src/pipeline.rs (reason_code - the strings CST_SHAPE_MISMATCH:targets, LEX_OVER_EMIT:call etc. come from here)

items.why_hard: the reference lexer emits right-nested x-events per call, so the moment a calls bucket is unmasked, every call demands a matching x-event chain. Files fall, rows multiply 2-10x, the rule forces a revert, and the knowledge of what the invariant actually is never gets captured. Nobody has written the invariant down, so each lane rediscovers it and loses the same attempts.
items.definition_of_done: a written statement of the x-event nesting rule (with a small fixture per language that asserts it), plus at least one language where unmasking calls drops files with flat rows - bash is the best candidate (1,681 files, 582 currently failing).
do_not: do not unmask a calls bucket without predicting the row delta from the event counts first
do not accept rows up on the grounds that files dropped

items.title: Grammar recovery swallows whole C blocks and no target covers it

evidence.c_corpus: CST_DEGRADED:recovery accounted for 128 of C's 554 fallback files in the 2026-11-16 sweep, and 137 of the 295 measured on 2026-11-17
evidence.rust: the same bucket holds 2 rust rows, both the same file: the source repeats a `fn` header line so the whole block sits in recovery and the call inside it has no CST node to be read from (CST_MISSING_KIND:call, 2 rows)

where.grammar: src/deep/ and the grammar tables; the CVD parser's error recovery
where.rust_bug: the repeated `fn` header case - a grammar gap, not a reader guard

items.why_hard: unsolved.md is explicit: 'error nodes are the CVD parser's recovery, not a reader disagreement, and the threshold is the only knob that is honest here'. Raising the budget hides the problem; fixing it means teaching recovery to resynchronise on the next item boundary instead of consuming the block.
items.definition_of_done: C below 200 fallback files (from 295) with the recovery threshold unchanged, the 7-corpus guard unchanged, and the repeated-fn-header fixture parsing with 0 rows.
do_not: do not raise the recovery budget or the parse budget to move the number

omitted_on_purpose.why: everything else on the board is a per-language reader fix that a lane can land without design work, so it is not worth this agent's usage
examples: PAIR_AMBIGUOUS:1 (no rust row, one ts row)
LEX_OVER_EMIT:name (1 rust row, fix belongs in src/expr.rs = H2's area)
